# Research Memo: Bilingual (AR-RTL / EN-LTR) React 19 + Vite + TS Frontend, 2026

> **Verification notice:** I had no live web access while writing this. I quoted each excerpt from memory of the cited page. URLs marked **UNVERIFIED** may have moved or changed wording. Before you cite any quote, re-fetch the page and confirm it byte-for-byte.

**Assumptions** (brief was ambiguous):
- A1: "2026 thresholds" means the currently published Core Web Vitals thresholds. I know of no announced 2026 change. **UNVERIFIED for 2026.**
- A2: The UI supports exactly two locales, `ar` and `en`, and switches direction for the whole document.
- A3: Quran/Hadith text is rendered from corpus IDs only. The frontend never transforms it (Constraint 1).
- A4: Lighthouse runs in CI using Lighthouse CI (`lhci`).

## Standard/Practice

- **Direction.** Set `lang` and `dir` on `<html>` per locale. Use `dir="auto"` or `<bdi>` for user-supplied or mixed fragments, such as an English query typed into the Arabic UI. This follows the W3C Internationalization guidance and the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm (UAX #9).
- **Layout.** Use CSS logical properties only (`margin-inline-start`, `padding-block`, `inset-inline-end`, `text-align: start`). This lets one stylesheet serve both directions.
- **Arabic typography.**
  - Self-host WOFF2 fonts with `font-display: swap` (or `optional`), subset with `unicode-range`, and preload the primary Arabic face.
  - Never apply `letter-spacing` to Arabic, because it breaks cursive joining. (Rationale is W3C Arabic layout guidance, not linked below; **UNVERIFIED**.)
- **Accessibility.** Target WCAG 2.2 Level AA. The new AA criteria that matter here are 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum), 2.5.7 Dragging Movements, 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum), and 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication. Language is covered by 3.1.1 and 3.1.2.
- **i18n.** With two locales and mostly static UI strings, typed plain JSON catalogs plus native `Intl.*` APIs are sufficient. Bring in a library such as react-i18next or FormatJS only if you need ICU plurals or lazy namespace loading. This is a judgment call, not a standard.
- **Testing.**
  - Vitest for unit and component tests.
  - Playwright for E2E tests in both locales.
  - `@axe-core/playwright` for automated accessibility scans.
- **Performance.**
  - Core Web Vitals "good" targets: LCP ≤ 2.5 s, INP ≤ 200 ms, CLS ≤ 0.1, measured at the 75th percentile.
  - Enforce these through Lighthouse CI assertions.

## Why it matters for this project

- **Bidi errors misrepresent citations.** Citation references mix Arabic text with Latin digits and IDs (e.g., "Bukhari 1"). Bidi mistakes can visually reorder these, which could misrepresent a citation.
- **The frontend must not alter religious text.** Constraint 1 requires byte-exact display. Fonts and CSS must render, never transform: no `text-transform`, no JS Unicode normalization, no "smart quotes".
- **Accessibility is core for the audience.** Elderly users and screen-reader users are core audiences for religious verification tools. WCAG 2.2 AA is the defensible baseline.
- **Fonts drive Core Web Vitals.** Large Arabic font files are the main LCP and CLS risk.

## Concrete rules (numbered, each testable/automatable)

1. In both locales, `<html>` has `lang` ∈ {`ar`,`en`} and `dir` ∈ {`rtl`,`ltr`}, set to match. Test with Playwright: `expect(page.locator('html')).toHaveAttribute('dir','rtl')`.
2. Stylelint rejects physical properties. Enable `stylelint-use-logical` (or an equivalent rule) to ban `margin-left/right`, `padding-left/right`, `left/right`, and `text-align: left|right`. CI fails on any violation.
3. Wrap every user-supplied or mixed-direction string in `<bdi>` or give it `dir="auto"`. Enforce with a component lint rule and a Playwright DOM assertion.
4. Corpus text is byte-exact in the DOM: rendered `textContent === corpus[id]`. The test runs over all fixture IDs in both locales.
5. Grep CI fails on `.normalize(` anywhere in the render path.
6. Computed style on any corpus-text or Arabic element has `letter-spacing: normal` and `text-transform: none`. Check with a Playwright `getComputedStyle` check.
7. All fonts are self-hosted WOFF2 with `font-display` ∈ {`swap`,`optional`}. The primary Arabic face has `<link rel="preload" as="font" crossorigin>`. A build-output test parses the CSS and HTML to confirm.
8. `@axe-core/playwright` reports zero violations tagged `wcag2a`, `wcag2aa`, `wcag21aa`, or `wcag22aa` on every route, in both locales.
9. Interactive targets are ≥ 24×24 CSS px (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8). A Playwright `boundingBox()` sweep checks all `button, a, [role=button], input`.
10. Focused elements are not fully hidden by sticky headers (SC 2.4.11). Run a Playwright tab-through test that checks intersection with the viewport minus header bounds.
11. The `ar.json` and `en.json` key sets are identical. A Vitest test diffs them, and TypeScript types are generated from `en.json`.
12. No hard-coded UI strings appear in JSX. Enforce with ESLint `i18next/no-literal-string` or an equivalent rule.
13. Dates and numbers are formatted only via `Intl.DateTimeFormat` and `Intl.NumberFormat` using the active locale. Enforce with a lint rule that bans manual formatting.
14. Lighthouse CI asserts, on mobile emulation:
    - `largest-contentful-paint` ≤ 2500 ms
    - `cumulative-layout-shift` ≤ 0.1
    - `total-blocking-time` ≤ 200 ms (lab proxy for INP)
    - accessibility category score = 1.0
15. Field data checks INP ≤ 200 ms, LCP ≤ 2.5 s, and CLS ≤ 0.1 at the 75th percentile, using `web-vitals` library reporting. Review is a release gate.
16. Vitest coverage thresholds are enforced in `vitest.config.ts`, including a 100% branch target for citation-display components.
17. Playwright runs Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit projects, each for both `ar` and `en`.
